newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 4.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- A consortium of U.S.-based SBC Communications SBC and Telkom Malaysia has succeeded in its bid for a 30 percent stake in South Africa's Telkom utility, kickstarting the country's first major privatisation exercise.

- The identity of security police informers under apartheid, including some some alleged to be high-ranking members of the African National Congress government, will not be disclosed at "truth commission" amnesty hearings despite a plea by Deputy President Thabo Mbeki that they be named.

- McCarthy Retail Ltd is to sell twenty six percent of McCarthy Motor Holdings to Imperial Holdings Ltd for 218 million rand and seek an independent Johannesburg Stock Exchange listing for the motor division "as soon as is practical".
- A fire gutted parts of Pretoria's main municipal building, causing damage estimated at millions of rand and destroying many computers and records, police said.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Telkom Malaysia and SBC Communications secured the bid for a 30 percent stake in South Africa's Telkom by default, as their consortium emerged as the sole contender for the strategic equity partner in the state telecomunications utility.
- Taxpayers stand to lose at least 180 million rand because of the government's now-abandoned policy of guaranteeing loans to gold mines in financial difficulty, figures released last week show.

- The Binani Group and Sterlite Industries (India) Ltd, two companies based in India, have joined the bid against South Africa's Avmin-led consortium for the most prized divisions of ZCCM, the troubled Zambian copper producer, Zambian government sources said.

- An agreement has been reached in principle to launch a new black-owned oil company called Naledi Petroleum. Main shareholers include the National Black Fuel Retailer Association and a consortium of black empowerment companies.
SAKE-BEELD

- Deputy President Thabo Mbeki said the state would have to maintain the integrity of procedures for awarding state contracts even as it reforms these to allow greater participation by black business.
- A consortium including SBC Communication and Telkom Malaysia is the final candidate as the strategic partner in South Africa's Telkom partial privatisation.
- Two of South Africa's biggest motor dealers are going to work in future together, with Imperial Holdings Ltd taking a 26-percent stake in McCarthy Motor Holdings.
THE STAR
- An 80-year-old farmer and two armed robbers died in a shootout when seven men attacked the farm east of Pretoria.
- The entire west wing of the Pretoria City Council's administration complex housing the tax, licensing, and water and electricity departments has been destroyed by fire.
- The price of water is set to go up by about 12 percent on April 1, Water Affairs Minister Kader Asmal announced.
